evidence.C1: The 'learner phase' (invincible car, no stars until first job done) guarantees a stranger completes the first job without frustration, and prompts like 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' are unambiguous.
evidence.C2: Strong mood with neon/glow pass and distinct districts (Sol Beach vs Rustport), but geometry remains simple blocks; Screenshot 8 (Sol Wheel at dusk) is recognizable, but day shots are plainer.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, five odd job types, cab fares, property, perks, and police helicopters all feed into money sinks and progression, creating high variety for a browser sandbox.
evidence.C4: Desktop HUD is minimal ('cash and health'), but mobile touch layout (Screenshot 15) is dense with 8+ buttons overlaying the view, potentially obscuring driving lines.
evidence.C5: The 'Not covered by the tests' section explicitly admits 'No real phone or tablet has run the game yet' and 'No real players have tried it yet', stating limits plainly.

fixes: Test touch controls on real mobile devices immediately; v1.5 relies on them but they are currently only emulated, risking usability issues with thumb reach and heat.
Tune Job 4 ('Borrowed Time') difficulty or police AI; the test script failed 1 of 3 runs due to arrests, suggesting a difficulty spike that may frustrate human players.
Reduce mobile HUD button density or opacity; Screenshot 15 shows large buttons covering significant screen real estate which could obscure obstacles during high-speed driving.

evidence.C1: Title screen shows 'HOW TO PLAY' with key bindings; learner phase prevents stars until first job done; first job ends at Sol Wheel landmark; 'A new player who stands still for 3.5 seconds is shown the walking keys'; route arrows on road and minimap guide player. Slight density on title screen keeps it from a 10.
evidence.C2: Four districts with distinct looks (Meridian towers, Sol Beach pastels, Rustport industry, suburbs); day/night cycle with lit windows, neon trim, moon; 86 painted walls; detailed building features (slanted crowns, balcony bands, saw-tooth roofs); Pretty graphics adds glow pass and vignette. Screenshots show recognizable mood but some elements remain blocky.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, five odd job types (Rush Order, Repo Run, Block Dash, Hot Parcel, Paper Round), cab fares, property buying, hidden packages, harbor courier, police with helicopter at 4 stars, Tune-up shop in three stages; perks tie activities together (5 packages = 25% less damage, 10 fares = double tips, all jobs = +50% rent). Rich interlocking systems.
evidence.C4: 'A quieter screen': HUD is cash and health; stars only when wanted; weapon line only 5s after change; clock moved to map/pause; pause screen is three buttons plus settings/perks; G8 passed no overlaps at 3 sizes; perk card shows progress ('Body armour 4/5'). Clean and contextual but not exceptional.
evidence.C5: Own city and names (Meridian, Sol Beach, Rustport, Sol Wheel, Coastliner); G9 passed own names only; title screen states 'not affiliated with the publisher or the series it is often compared to'; fact sheet honestly states 'No real players have tried it yet', 'No real phone or tablet has run the game yet', and what script tests cannot measure.

fixes: Get real player testing to validate difficulty curves and fun factor — script tests show job 4 (Borrowed Time) failed 1 of 3 runs and the 1.5 run of job 1 broke with a browser hang; a script cannot say whether a job is fun.

Test touch controls on real phones/tablets — fact sheet admits 'No real phone or tablet has run the game yet, so thumb reach, heat and frame rate on a phone are not known'; this is a major untested surface for the 1.5 'Pocket' release.

Simplify the title screen to reduce information density for first-time players — the current screen packs settings, controls list, release history link, and not-affiliated line into one view, which could overwhelm a stranger in the first minute.

evidence.C1: 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' with 'JOB 335 m', road arrows and a landmark ending; learner phase means 'crimes bring no stars' and the car 'cannot be wrecked'. But job 1 takes '38.5 to 50.9 s' even for a script, so a stranger likely exceeds 60 s, and the title HOW TO PLAY panel must be read first.
evidence.C2: The Sol Wheel dusk shot (neon wheel, palms, pink sky) and the night light pools are distinctive, and districts have own palettes; but the Rustport quay is flat 'container stacks' and the downtown facades stay generic, so not every single screenshot is recognisable as this world.
evidence.C3: Perks 'tie the side activities together' (packages to damage/respray, fares to tips, jobs to rent), the wheel ride 'marks the three nearest unfound packages', heat closes shops and refuses fares. Residual: secrets are only 15 packages, and the races/getaway 'difficulty and their time limits are not measured'.
evidence.C4: 'the HUD is cash and health; the stars appear only when you are wanted'; G8 'no overlaps at 3 sizes'; pause is 'three buttons, settings and perks'. Residual: the always-on perk card ('Body armour 4 / 5') and the denser stacked phone HUD are the only clutter.
evidence.C5: 'Own city, names and art' plus the one not-affiliated line; limits stated plainly: 'No real players have tried it yet. The scores are from AI judges.' Residual: the neon-Miami look is genre-familiar rather than wholly its own.

fixes: Re-run test/drive.py on 1.5 - the job 1 run 'broke with a browser hang and gave no result' - then human-time a real stranger through the first job to prove the sub-60-second first minute.
Test the new touch controls on a real phone or tablet (thumb reach, heat, frame rate); so far only an emulated phone has run it and the WebKit check was skipped.
Give the plainer views (Rustport quay's flat container stacks, generic downtown facades) the same signature identity as the Sol Wheel dusk shot so any one screenshot reads as Neon Coast.
